title: "Guaranteed" Double Your Money
subject: Retirees: DOUBLE your savings in 90 days — guaranteed!
body:
Dear Valued Investor,

Our exclusive AI trading program has delivered guaranteed returns of 100% in just 90 days for hundreds of retirees just like you. ZERO RISK.

Only 12 spots remain this month. Secure your spot today with a minimum investment of $5,000.

ACT NOW before this opportunity closes!
redFlags: "Guaranteed" returns and "zero risk"
Doubling your money in 90 days
Limited spots and pressure to act now
Targets retirees by name
explanation: Every real investment carries risk, and nobody can guarantee you'll double your money. "Act now" pressure keeps you from checking the company out.
howToSpot: Any guarantee of high returns means scam. Look up the company and the person at brokercheck.finra.org and investor.gov before investing anything.

title: Trading App Won't Let You Withdraw
subject: Withdrawal notice
body:
Your account balance: $48,200.00 (+382%)

Withdrawal request: $48,200.00
Status: ON HOLD

To complete your withdrawal, a 20% capital gains tax ($9,640) must be paid in advance. Please deposit the tax amount in USDT cryptocurrency within 3 days. Accounts with unpaid tax will be frozen and funds forfeited.
redFlags: Enormous gains in a short time
Must pay "taxes" or "fees" to get your own money
Payment demanded in cryptocurrency
Threat that your funds will be frozen
explanation: The balance is fake. It's just numbers on a website the scammers control. The money you deposited is already gone. Paying the "tax" only adds to the loss.
howToSpot: Real platforms take any fees out of your balance. They never make you send more money to withdraw. Stop paying and report it at ic3.gov.

title: Told to Pay at a Bitcoin ATM
sender: Caller claiming to be your "account protection advisor"
subject: Phone call
body: "Your bank account has been hacked and the hackers are draining it right now. You need to withdraw $12,000 in cash and take it to the Bitcoin ATM at the gas station on Route 9. I'll stay on the phone with you and give you a QR code to scan so your money goes into a secure wallet. Don't tell the bank teller why you're withdrawing it. They may be part of the hack."
redFlags: Told to put cash into a Bitcoin ATM
Stays on the phone the whole time
Tells you to lie to the bank teller
Claims bank staff are part of the problem
explanation: No real bank, business, or government agency will ever tell you to put money into a Bitcoin ATM. Once the money goes into the scammer's QR code, it's almost impossible to get back.
howToSpot: Hang up the moment anyone mentions a Bitcoin ATM. Tell the bank teller the truth. They're trained to spot these scams and want to help.

title: Social Media "Mentor" Group
sender: "Professor Alan Grant – Wealth Mentor" on WhatsApp
subject: Group chat invitation
body:
Welcome to my private VIP investing group! 🎉 Members made an average of 35% profit last week following my stock signals. See screenshots below from happy members!

Today's free tip will be posted at 2 PM. VIP members who join our new platform get my premium signals. Spaces are limited.
redFlags: Invites you to a private chat group
Screenshots of profits (easy to fake)
"Free tips" that lead to a paid platform
Limited spaces create pressure
explanation: Many "members" in these groups are scammers or fake accounts cheering each other on. After a few free tips, they move you to a fake investing platform where your deposits disappear.
howToSpot: Real advisors don't recruit through WhatsApp groups. Check anyone offering investment advice at brokercheck.finra.org.

title: Statement Notice from Your Own Brokerage
sender: Your brokerage <no-reply@yourbrokerage.com> (the company you already use)
subject: Your quarterly statement is ready
body:
Hello Margaret,

Your statement for July–September is now available. To view it, sign in to your account using our app or by typing our website address into your browser.

For your security, we will never ask for your password or a verification code by email or phone.

Questions? Call the number on the back of your statement.
explanation: This is a normal notice from a company you already do business with. It uses your name, doesn't rush you, doesn't ask for money or information, and tells you to sign in the way you normally do.
howToSpot: Even with real emails, sign in through the app or a website address you type yourself, not through a link.

title: "We Can Recover Your Lost Money"
subject: We located your lost crypto funds
body:
Dear Victim,

Our investigators have traced the $36,000 you lost to an online trading scam. Working with international law enforcement, we can return 100% of your funds within 10 days.

To begin the recovery process, a refundable retainer of $2,500 is required. Please reply to begin.

Asset Recovery Legal Group
redFlags: Contacts you after you've lost money to a scam
Promises to get back 100% of your money
Upfront "retainer" fee
Claims to work with "international law enforcement"
explanation: This is a recovery scam, often run by the same criminals who took your money the first time. Law enforcement never charges fees to recover stolen money.
howToSpot: Report losses at ic3.gov and reportfraud.ftc.gov, which are free. Never pay anyone who promises to recover lost money.
